messages:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed a strange behavior from /v1/embeddings when clients send mixed null/empty values in a batch. Response length matches non-nulls but ordering looks shifted. Anyone seen this?
Ian: Which client and model? JS or Python?
Maya: JS SDK, batch ~512 items. Payload included null and empty string values.
Sanjay: I vaguely remember a gateway optimization that strips empty items before batching. Could be that.
Emily: Can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) and the model name?
Maya: snippet: ```json {"input": ["hello", null, "", "very long text..."], "model": "text-embed-legacy"} ```
Ian: Per our API contract we should preserve input order and return one embedding slot per input. Historically we accepted nulls but didn't clearly define response mapping.
Sanjay: Two approaches: 1) Reject nulls with 400 (strict), or 2) Accept nulls and return explicit `null` entries in the embeddings array to preserve positional mapping.
Rachel: I'd vote for option 2 for backward compatibility — many clients send optional content. Throwing 400 could break them.
Maya: Agree. Implementation-wise we can short-circuit null/empty inputs and return null vectors for null, a real vector for "" (embedding of empty string).
Sam: I'll implement a runtime helper to map inputs -> calls: filter only non-null to the model, then re-insert nulls into the result. Small patch.
Emily: Also flag: we observed inconsistent vector dimensionality across variants (1024 vs 1536) for the same named model. Should we include model dimension in the response to avoid consumer parsing issues?
Ian: Model catalog documents dims, but including `metadata.model_dimensions` in the response would be helpful for clients that don't pin to catalog. Minimal change: add `model_dimensions` on the top-level response or per-embedding.
Rachel: Per-embedding gives clarity when mixed-model fallbacks happen. Example: [{"embedding": [...], "model": "...", "model_dimensions": 1536}, null, ...]
Maya: That looks good. Keep payload size reasonable — dimension is a small integer.
Sanjay: Another question: truncation rules. Is truncation per-item token limit or do we have a total-batch token cap?
Ian: Current behavior: per-item truncation at ~8192 tokens and per-request item count cap (512). No cross-item token accounting.
Maya: That should be explicitly documented. We had a customer assuming we truncate across the entire batch which led to surprising embeddings.
Emily: Test matrix for PRs: ordering retained, null -> null mapping, empty-string handled, per-item truncation unit test, batch size enforcement, dims in response, mixed model fallback behavior.
Sam: I'll add unit + integration tests. Planning to land runtime helper (PR #5743) and gateway compatibility shim (PR #5742).
Maya: PRs are up for review, pinging reviewers. Quick review pls — we want to canary before EOD.
Sam: I'll review after lunch, unless @Rachel wants to take an early look.
Rachel: I'll glance at gateway PR now.
prod-bot: Deploy note: gateway canary scheduled 14:00 UTC if PRs merged; runtime helper will go to canary after gateway is healthy.
Maya: Thanks — I'll also update docs with explicit examples for nulls vs empty strings and add a short FAQ for support. :thumbsup:
Ian: One more: decide on HTTP semantics for nulls — prefer null in response body over 204/partial success. Agree?
Sanjay: Agree, 200 with explicit null entries is clearer for client libraries.
Maya: Cool. I'll file a tiny spec update and attach it to the PRs.
Emily: Leaving a checklist in the PR description for QA to run.
Sam: If anything blocks me, I'll @Maya.
Maya: Closing loop — thanks everyone.
